h1: The 8 Best Printers for College Students of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: the 8 best printers for college students, covering inkjet, laser, and portable options for dorm rooms and shared apartments.
summary: The HP DeskJet 4355 is our best all-rounder for mixed coursework. The Canon PIXMA TS4320 suits art and design majors who need color and duplex printing, and the Brother HL-L2405W is the pick for text-heavy majors. The Canon TR4720 handles multi-page scanning, and the MT610Pro portable printer fits students who mostly use library printers.
intro: The cheapest printer in a dorm is rarely the cheapest to own. Students pick a low sticker price, then run through ink or toner during finals week and wonder why every page costs so much. The better question is what you print: essays, color posters, or scanned problem sets.

We reviewed eight printers on paper, comparing technology, features like duplex and auto document feeders, and how well each fits a small dorm desk. The ranking favors versatility for mixed coursework, then rewards specialists in their niche.

products.name: HP DeskJet 4355 Wireless All-in-One Color Inkjet Printer
products.verdict: The most flexible compact printer for a general student.
products.description:
The DeskJet 4355 is a wireless color inkjet that prints, scans, and copies from a compact body. It comes with a 3-month Instant Ink trial, which can lower ink costs early on, and it sits in the $50 to $100 bracket.

It ranks first because it covers every basic need without specializing, while the Canon TS4320 adds duplex but is aimed at color-heavy work. This one is the one to buy before you know your major's demands.

Buy it if you are undeclared or print a mix of essays and the odd color page. The caveat is that inkjet cartridges still cost over time.
products.idealFor: Undeclared or general education students with mixed needs.
products.skipIf: You print hundreds of text pages a month.

products.name: Canon PIXMA TS4320 Wireless Color Inkjet Printer
products.verdict: Duplex printing makes it the best pick for visual coursework.
products.description:
The TS4320 is a wireless color inkjet that prints, copies, and scans, and it adds duplex printing so you can print on both sides. It carries a 1-year limited warranty and sits in the $50 to $100 range.

It ranks second because duplex saves paper on long readings, a feature the HP DeskJet lacks. The HP wins overall only because its Instant Ink trial and broader appeal edge it out.

Buy it if you are in art, design, or any major that prints in color. The caveat is the same inkjet running cost as the HP.
products.idealFor: Art and design students who print in color.

products.name: Brother HL-L2405W Wireless Compact Monochrome Laser Printer
products.verdict: A black-and-white laser for students who print a lot of text.
products.description:
The HL-L2405W is a compact monochrome laser printer with wireless and mobile printing support, and it works with Alexa. It includes a Refresh Subscription trial and sits in the $100 to $200 range.

It ranks third because it is a print-only machine, with no scanning or copying, and no color. The inkjets above are more flexible, but laser toner usually suits heavy text printing better.

Buy it if you read many PDFs and print them. The caveat is that you cannot scan or print color.

products.name: Canon PIXMA TR4720 All-in-One Wireless Printer
products.verdict: An auto document feeder for multi-page scanning.
products.description:
The TR4720 is a wireless all-in-one with an auto document feeder, built-in fax, mobile printing support, and print, scan, and copy functions. It comes in white and sits in the $50 to $100 range.

It ranks fourth because the feeder is a real advantage for multi-page scanning, but students rarely need fax, and the TS4320 offers duplex that this one does not list.

Buy it if you scan problem sets or signed forms often. The caveat is that fax is an unneeded extra.
products.idealFor: Students who scan many pages or signed documents.
products.skipIf: You only print and never scan.

products.name: Canon PIXMA TS3720 Wireless All-in-One Printer
products.verdict: A light, basic printer for occasional printing.
products.description:
The TS3720 is a wireless color inkjet all-in-one focused on basic home printing, with a compact, lightweight body. It prints, scans, and copies, and it is priced at $50 to $100.

Fifth place reflects that it has no duplex, no feeder, and no trial ink plan, so it offers less than the picks above. It is lightweight, which suits a dorm that gets moved each semester.

Buy it for light printing needs. The caveat is that it does not stand out in any feature.
products.idealFor: Students with light, general printing needs.
products.skipIf: You want duplex or a feeder.

products.name: Canon Pixma MG3620 Wireless All-in-One Color Inkjet Printer
products.verdict: Mobile and tablet printing suits locked-down laptops.
products.description:
The MG3620 is a wireless color inkjet all-in-one with mobile and tablet printing support, in a black compact desktop design. It sits in the $100 to $200 range.

It ranks sixth because it costs more than the TS3720 and TS4320 yet lists no extra feature beyond mobile printing. That mobile support is what suits a school-issued Chromebook.

Buy it if your laptop blocks driver installs. The caveat is the higher price for modest specs.
products.idealFor: Students with a Chromebook or restricted laptop.
products.skipIf: You want the best value for the money.

products.name: Inkless Portable Printer for Travel (MT610Pro)
products.verdict: No ink or toner, but it only does thermal prints.
products.description:
The MT610Pro is a Bluetooth inkless thermal printer that supports 8.5 by 11 inch Letter and A4 at 300 DPI. It works with iOS, Android, and laptops and uses no cartridges, in the $50 to $100 range.

It ranks seventh because thermal prints are monochrome and it does not scan or copy, so it replaces a full printer only for light use. The tradeoff is zero ink cost.

Buy it if you mostly use library printers and need an occasional page. The caveat is the limited output type.
products.idealFor: Students with very light printing needs.
products.skipIf: You need scanning or regular color prints.

products.name: Canon TS6420 All-in-One Wireless Printer
products.verdict: A fuller control panel for shared use.
products.description:
The TS6420 is a wireless color inkjet all-in-one with a fuller control panel layout, in a black compact desktop body. It prints, scans, and copies, and costs more than the TS4320 for the extra panel.

It ranks last because the spec sheet lists no standout feature beyond that panel. The panel does help when several people share the machine.

Buy it if you split a printer with roommates. The caveat is that you pay more for convenience.
products.skipIf: You are buying alone on a tight budget.

whatMatters.detail: Inkjets print color and photos well but cartridges run out and dry up with disuse. Laser printers use toner and suit lots of black text. Decide based on whether you print color; the listing names the technology in the title.
Duplex means automatic two-sided printing, which halves paper use on long readings. Many cheap printers lack it. Look for 'duplex' or 'auto two-sided' on the spec sheet.
A feeder scans multi-page stacks without lifting the lid each time. It matters for problem sets or contracts. Check the listing for 'ADF' or 'auto document feeder'.
Locked-down laptops often block driver installs. Mobile printing support lets you print from a phone or browser instead. Look for wireless and mobile printing in the bullets.
The purchase price is only part of the cost; ink or toner is the rest. Trials like Instant Ink can help early on. Check which cartridges the model uses and whether a subscription fits your volume.

cards.label: Inkjet
cards.text: Inkjets print color and scan or copy in one body. The HP DeskJet 4355, Canon TS4320, TR4720, TS3720, MG3620, and TS6420 are inkjets.

cards.label: Laser
cards.text: A monochrome laser suits heavy text printing and uses toner. The Brother HL-L2405W is the only laser here, but it prints black and white only.

howToChoose.note: Most students should default to inkjet unless they print mostly black text in volume.

cards.label: In this ranking
cards.text: The Canon PIXMA TS3720 is lightweight and compact, and the HP DeskJet 4355 adds a compact design with more flexibility.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: You print daily text readings, where the Brother laser's toner suits you better than inkjet cartridges.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: You print only occasionally, where the Canon TS3720 or the inkless MT610Pro are enough.

faq.q: Does a printer work with a Chromebook?
faq.a: Many do via wireless and mobile printing. The Canon MG3620 lists mobile and tablet support, which helps on locked-down laptops. Confirm compatibility on the listing.

faq.q: What mistake do students make buying printers?
faq.a: Buying on sticker price alone. Ink or toner is the ongoing cost, so match the technology to what you print.

faq.q: Is a laser worth it over an inkjet?
faq.a: Only if you print lots of black text. The Brother laser can't do color, scanning, or copying.

faq.q: How do I set up a wireless printer?
faq.a: Connect it to your Wi-Fi from the control panel or app, then add it to your laptop or phone. Dorm networks sometimes restrict this, so ask your IT office.

faq.q: How do I keep inkjet ink from drying?
faq.a: Print something short every week or two. Long idle gaps cause cartridges to clog.

faq.q: Can I rely on a portable thermal printer?
faq.a: For occasional black pages, yes. The MT610Pro prints at 300 DPI on Letter and A4 but does not scan or copy.

finalTake: The HP DeskJet 4355 is the safest all-round buy for a student whose print needs are still unknown. Pick the Canon TS4320 for color and duplex, or the Brother laser for text-heavy majors. Match the machine to your workload, because the ink or toner bill is what you will actually notice.
